Drop chancegame term · verified
Each enemy drop has a drop chance, written as a number out of 10,000. You get the drop when a random number from 0 to 9,999 is below that number (at the normal rate of 100). So 100 = 1%. An enemy gives only one reward.

Capture · verified and estimate parts are marked
What it is: Capture is a state you put on the enemy. If it is still on the enemy when you win the fight, the chance that the enemy drops its capture item rises from about 1% to about 10%. Its normal drops do not change. Without Capture the capture item stays at about 1%.
✔ verified: Capture is the only thing that raises the capture item chance (1% to 10%). Disaster bosses have capture items, and so do dungeon bosses, conquest bosses and most special bosses.
Three ways to put Capture on a boss:
1. Skill Spider Snare, burst form (Capture Net): targets the enemy, hit value 100, lasts the whole combat, quick action, costs 4 Brave, cooldown 5.
2. Job Scholar: its Arresting state puts Capture on the enemy when you land a crit (hit value 100, lasts 1 combat).
3. Skill runes: Capture (Weak) (150% ailment hit, lasts 1 turn) and Capture (Strong) (150% ailment hit, lasts 5 turns or 1 room). They trigger when you use that skill directly.
~ estimate: the state is still on the boss at the moment you win. This is not confirmed, so a source that lasts longer is safer: Capture (Strong) or the whole-combat Capture Net beat the 1-turn rune.
~ estimate: Capture is an ailment, so the usual ailment rule applies: skill value + your Effective - the boss's Resist, limited to 5..95%. Even a hit value of 150 can miss, so raise your Effective.
Not known yet: whether disaster bosses can resist Capture, and what the capture item actually does.

Star rarity (6★ and 7★ drops) · verified rules, odds are examples
Short answer: no Item Rarity amount unlocks 6★ or 7★. The ceiling comes from your run (Risk and Progress), not from the stat.
Skills, runes and equipment: 6★ and 7★ only roll in risk mode (Risk 100 or more, called Savage mode in the guide). Without it the top is 5★. Risk 1000 or more adds +1 star to the roll (Risk can only go past 999 with a special effect that lifts the limit).
Treasure chest items: the top depends on Progress: 2★ under 20, 3★ under 80, 4★ under 140, then 5★. In risk mode: 6★ from Progress 200 and 7★ from Progress 500.
What Item Rarity does: it only gives extra chances at +1 star on chest items, up to that ceiling. Equipment Rarity, Skill Rarity and Rune Rarity do the same for their own picks. Reroll power adds more tries (see the reroll answer).
Example odds (chest, Progress 600, Risk 100): at an internal value of 0 / 20 / 50 about 3%, 4.5% and 13% for a 6★ or 7★. At Risk 1000: about 12%, 16% and 30%.
Not known yet: how the in-game Item Rarity number (+1) matches the internal value used in the odds, and how much Progress each room or floor gives (the Risk gains are in the Risk answer). Risk and Progress are the names used here, so check the wording in the game.

Riskgame term · part unverified
A run counter, written as a % in the game text (Risk 100 = 100%). At 100% or more you are in risk mode, where 6 and 7 stars can appear (6 from Progress 200, 7 from Progress 500).
The limit is 999%. A special effect that lifts the limit allows up to 9999%, and only then can Risk reach 1000% or more, which gives a roll +1 star.
It goes up by 3% after every won fight, by 3% more if the enemy was an elite, and by 2% when you enter a dark room. Going from under 100% to 100% or more adds a one-time +50%. Lost fights give no Risk.
It goes down by 2% for each new room, and by 2% for each new floor and 15% at a camp.
Part of this is unverified: the 3% per won fight is likely on the Android version but not proved, and when the floor and camp changes run was not traced. Some events and effects add or remove Risk too.
Source Rules R52, R69 and a guide check · verified; one part unverified
How drops and rarity work

Damage over Timeterm
At the start of their turn, target will receive damage of the corresponding type. There are three types of damage: Bleed, Burn and Poison. The effect lasts for 5 turns under normal circumstances.

Delayed Damageterm
When the effect is applied, the target takes damage of the corresponding type after 3 turns.
There are three types of damage: Explosion, Frostbite and Curse. If the effect is cleansed or combat ends before it activates, the damage will not be received.

Reflect Damageterm
Whenever you receive direct damage, you will deal corresponding elemental damage. There are three types of damage: Thorns, Electrified and Retaliation. The effect lasts for 5 turns under normal circumstances.

Pursuit Damageterm
Whenever you deal direct damage of a certain type, you will deal additional damage of the corresponding type. There are three types of damage: Hidden Blade, Light Bullet and Erosion. The effect lasts for 5 turns under normal circumstances.

HP stackgame term · verified
An extra life. Every fight starts with full stacks. When a hit leaves you at 0 HP, one stack is spent (a Guts roll can keep it) and HP refills to max. You are dead at 0 HP with no stacks. Stacks are not scaled by 0.85.
Source Rules R04, R34 to R36 · verified

Guts · verified rules
Guts chance: your Guts stat, limited to 0 to 95%. The game rolls a random number from 0 to 99 and you keep the stack if it is below your chance. So a stack is never 100% safe.
When it matters: when you would spend an HP stack at 0 HP. A successful Guts roll keeps the stack. Otherwise one stack is spent. Either way your HP is refilled to max.
Where Guts comes from: gear (15 to 30), a few states, one enemy type and elites.
Not known yet: your exact Guts number in a run depends on your gear and states, so check them in the game.

Reset effectgame term · verified
Short for the Reset HP stack effect. It sets your HP stacks to the maximum and does not change HP or shield. It needs a hit on a living target. Camp, one gear effect and Call Miracle do it, and Call Miracle affects both sides.

Runes that steer which skill the game picks when it chooses for you (confused or auto). Cooldownterm
Skill cannot be used again until a certain number of turns have passed after it is used. This number of turns is called the cooldown. There are also status effects that can change the cooldown of skills.
In addition, there is also Stun, which causes skills to be put on cooldown.

Guts · verified rules
Guts chance: your Guts stat, limited to 0 to 95%. The game rolls a random number from 0 to 99 and you keep the stack if it is below your chance. So a stack is never 100% safe.
When it matters: when you would spend an HP stack at 0 HP. A successful Guts roll keeps the stack. Otherwise one stack is spent. Either way your HP is refilled to max.
Where Guts comes from: gear (15 to 30), a few states, one enemy type and elites.
Not known yet: your exact Guts number in a run depends on your gear and states, so check them in the game.

Parry chance = the attacker's "target parry" modifiers applied over (the target's parry modifiers applied over the target's Parry stat), limited to 0..95.
A parry only happens on direct attacks (damage becomes 0, "Parry!" shows). Against status effects only DEBUFFS can be parried, never buffs. Several effects cannot be parried (Stone Bind, Slow, Entangle Root, Storm Bind and others). Some effects make nobody able to parry.

Riskgame term · part unverified
A run counter, written as a % in the game text (Risk 100 = 100%). At 100% or more you are in risk mode, where 6 and 7 stars can appear (6 from Progress 200, 7 from Progress 500).
The limit is 999%. A special effect that lifts the limit allows up to 9999%, and only then can Risk reach 1000% or more, which gives a roll +1 star.
It goes up by 3% after every won fight, by 3% more if the enemy was an elite, and by 2% when you enter a dark room. Going from under 100% to 100% or more adds a one-time +50%. Lost fights give no Risk.
It goes down by 2% for each new room, and by 2% for each new floor and 15% at a camp.
Part of this is unverified: the 3% per won fight is likely on the Android version but not proved, and when the floor and camp changes run was not traced. Some events and effects add or remove Risk too.

answers.q: should I reroll or take the pick
answers.a:
Reroll or take the pick? · rules verified, advice is an estimate
What a reroll does: rarity rolls use your run Progress and Risk. The upper limit is 5 stars (7 in risk mode, where 6 and 7 stars need risk mode).
Reroll power N: gives N extra tries for +1 star. Sources: the enhanced-reroll state, three origins, and buying a shop reroll contract (levels 1 / 3 / 5 / 7), which overwrites your current power.
Minimum rarity: some pick screens require a minimum rarity, set by the effect that made them.
~ estimate: reroll when the pick is below the 5-star limit (7 in risk mode) and you have reroll power to spend. If the pick is already at the limit, extra tries cannot raise it, so take it.
Not known yet: the full cost of a plain reroll is not in this guide.

Armorgame rule · computed
Damage has three types: physical (P), magic (M), void (V), each with its own armor.
Armor is a percent cut, limited to 75. States that raise the armor cap (Iron wall, Sanctuary, Mutation) lift the limit to 95. Negative armor ADDS damage.
A crit ignores POSITIVE armor. Penetrate runes (P / M / V) ignore armor of that type. Penetration is subtracted from the target's armor.

answers.q: how do I get more skills
answers.a:
Getting more and better skills · verified rules, advice is an estimate
Where skills come from: pick screens. Their rarity is rolled from your run Progress and Risk, up to 5 stars (7 in risk mode).
Better picks: reroll power gives extra tries for +1 star (see the reroll answer). Some effects set a minimum rarity on a pick screen.
~ estimate: the surest way to see higher-rarity skills is to push Progress and, if you can survive it, risk mode. For cheap early skills that heal, shield or escape, ask: How do I survive a long run with low HP?
Not known yet: how many pick screens a run gives, and which rooms give a skill pick.

Tanky build · verified rules, advice is an estimate
HP stacks: not scaled by the 0.85 step. A spent stack refills your HP to max, and Guts (up to 95%) can keep the stack. Reset HP stack effects (Camp, a gear effect, Call Miracle) fill stacks to max.
Armor: a percent cut limited to 75 for each damage type (physical, magic, void). States such as Iron wall, Sanctuary and Mutation lift the limit to 95.
Parry: chance limited to 0 to 95% and only works on direct attacks, never on buffs. Sources: shields and the parry gear effect (15 per gear rarity), a few runes and skills.
~ estimate: a stack-based tank (many HP stacks plus Guts) beats raw max HP when enemies hit hard, because every stack is a full refill. Armor past the cap does nothing.

answers.q: which is better for a tank, tsukuyomi or queen's dress
answers.a:
Tanky build · verified rules, advice is an estimate
HP stacks: not scaled by the 0.85 step. A spent stack refills your HP to max, and Guts (up to 95%) can keep the stack. Reset HP stack effects (Camp, a gear effect, Call Miracle) fill stacks to max.
Armor: a percent cut limited to 75 for each damage type (physical, magic, void). States such as Iron wall, Sanctuary and Mutation lift the limit to 95.
Parry: chance limited to 0 to 95% and only works on direct attacks, never on buffs. Sources: shields and the parry gear effect (15 per gear rarity), a few runes and skills.
~ estimate: a stack-based tank (many HP stacks plus Guts) beats raw max HP when enemies hit hard, because every stack is a full refill. Armor past the cap does nothing.
